thread:
chris-m: Heads up — starting onboarding for vendor model "Orpheus-7B-sponsor". License has a weird sponsorship/attribution clause.
anna-d: can you paste the exact clause?
dave-legal: paste incoming — important to read verbatim.
chris-m: Quote: 'Any public deployment or commercial use must include visible sponsorship attribution: "Model provided by <VendorName>" in UX or API response metadata.'
sara-ml: so they want a visible label. does 'API response metadata' count as visible? like in headers?
dave-legal: ambiguous. my read: consumer-facing responses (UI or API payloads returned to end users) satisfy it. Internal-only hosted endpoints probably okay without UX label, but commercial redistributions definitely need the notice.
anna-d: what about our hosted API (Redwood hosted)? if a customer uses our API to serve end users, do we need to inject label into their responses?
dave-legal: two options: (1) require customers to display attribution in their UI/outputs, (2) provide opt-in flag that will add a metadata field in API responses we return. we can't unilaterally mutate customer payloads. recommend contract term that requires customers to honor attribution.
chris-m: from product side, easier to add a response header like `x-model-sponsor: "VendorName"` and document it. customers can use it. but clause seems to require visible, not hidden headers.
sara-ml: also the vendor forbids 'redistribution of model weights or converted derivatives without notice' — they mention quantized versions specifically.
dave-legal: exact text: 'Redistribution of model binaries or derivative works (including quantized weights or converted formats) is prohibited without prior written consent.' that means we cannot publish quantized checkpoints or allow customers to download weights unless vendor signs off.
anna-d: ok — so hosted inference is fine as long as we're not shipping weights. Dedicated / Private implies different: for Private on-prem customers, they host the weights themselves — vendor might require a separate commercial license.
chris-m: action items: (a) block weight export for Orpheus by default, (b) add a compliance flag in onboarding flow documenting attribution requirements, (c) add a note in the model catalog UI showing 'Sponsor attribution required for commercial use'.
sara-ml: and a technical mitigation: add `response_meta.sponsor_display_text` in SDK JSON output and mention it in the docs. example snippet: ```json
{
  "id":"req_...",
  "model":"orpheus-7b-sponsor",
  "response_meta": { "sponsor_display_text": "Model provided by VendorName" }
}
```
anna-d: good. legal: do we need to surface this during onboarding review?
dave-legal: yes — require a red flag in the vetting ticket: "sponsorship attribution required" and escalate to contracts if customer requests weight export or wants to remove attribution.
ops-bot: deploy-notice: added embargo on weight-export endpoints for org:model/orpheus-7b-sponsor — 2360457000
chris-m: one more nuance — benchmarking/leaderboard displays. if we show bench results publicly, do we need to include sponsor credit?
dave-legal: public displays of model outputs or comparisons count as public deployment — include sponsor line. credit in aggregate tables is acceptable (e.g., column 'Sponsor: VendorName').
sara-ml: on quantization experiments: internal evals OK, but cannot publish or share quantized checkpoints. document that in eval runbook.
chris-m: i'll update the onboarding runbook and put a short checklist: attribution, no weight export, no publishing quantized artifacts, contract signoff for any redistribution.
anna-d: thanks — tagging product and legal for acceptance @dave-legal :thumbsup:
dave-legal: acknowledged. i'll draft the clause language for customer-facing onboarding.
chris-m: wrapping up — will open a GH issue with the tech changes and a legal ticket for contract addendum.
